output.summary: An annual broadleaf plant native to the Mediterranean basin, bur clover commonly grows in farmland, roadsides and other disturbed ground. Its small yellow flowers are followed by tightly coiled, prickly pods that cling to clothing and animal fur, while its sprawling stems often root where they touch the ground. It is eaten as a vegetable, primarily in parts of eastern China, and by Indigenous Otomanguean communities in southern Mexico.
